correctness.rationale: Writing the resolvent as (1+dc)^(-1) times the positive adjacency Neumann series proves off-diagonal strict positivity for c>0 by connectedness. C=2R-I and translation invariance reduce nonnegativity to the common diagonal; the Fourier diagonal strictly falls from 1 to n^(-d)<1/2. Adding a coordinate strictly reduces the mean resolvent for c>0. The Laplace integrand factorizes; A_n(z)=I_0(z)+2 sum_{l>=1} I_{ln}(z). The Bessel ratio tends to zero at z=0 and obeys r'_m=1-r_m^2-(2m+1)r_m/z, preventing any first crossing of 1 by the negative derivative there. Termwise comparison gives the strict n ordering, and Riemann-sum convergence brackets the limiting root at every fixed d. Strict Jensen uses E Y=1 and Var(Y)=1/2 for n>=3 and for continuous angles. The one-dimensional kernel has q=e^-omega, cosh(omega)=1+1/c and diagonal (1+q^n)/[(1-q^n)sqrt(1+2c)]; at c=3/2, q=1/3 and the excess over 1/2 is epsilon/(1-epsilon) for epsilon=3^-n. Uniform derivative convergence on a compact root neighborhood first gives displacement O(epsilon); then q(c)^n=epsilon(1+O(n epsilon)) there, yielding coefficient 8. The finite 3-by-3 multiplicities for sum frequencies 0,3/2,3 are 1,4,4, giving 7c^2-c-2=0. The continuous square-lattice Haar change of variables gives the squared central-binomial moments and K in modulus convention. Independent AGM evaluation reproduced 0.5881972836856281148591326751..., and finite frequency calculations checked the radicals. For the dimension law, on compact t=dc intervals the cubic Taylor expansion and fourth moment control give Phi=1/(1+t)+t^2/[2d(1+t)^3]+O(d^-2), uniformly in n; bounded centered summands with variance 1/2 give signed third and fourth moments O(d^-2). Evaluating at fixed points around 1 first traps the root; then the derivative -1/4 at 1 and correction 1/(16d) imply t=1+1/(4d)+O(d^-2). The package's artifacts/verify.py and recorded output are corroborative finite evidence, including some floating-point checks; all strict inequalities for unbounded n,d rest on the analytic proof.
